chunks: From him, from al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from ʿAbbād ibn Ṣuhayb, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“The apostate is asked to repent; if he repents, otherwise he is killed.” He said: “And the woman is asked to repent; if she repents, otherwise she is imprisoned in the prison and hardship is inflicted upon her.”

key_terms.أُضِرَّ بِهَا: hardship was inflicted upon her; harm or severity was imposed upon her
key_terms.السِّجْنِ: the prison; the place of confinement
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman; here, the female apostate
key_terms.الْمُرْتَدُّ: the apostate; one who has turned back from the religion
key_terms.تَابَ: he repented; he returned from apostasy
key_terms.حُبِسَتْ: she was imprisoned; she was confined
key_terms.قُتِلَ: he was killed; the prescribed penalty was carried out
key_terms.يُسْتَتَابُ: is asked to repent; is called to return through tawbah

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām narrate about the ruling on a male and female apostate after being asked to repent?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the apostate man and woman, distinguishing between their prescribed treatment after being called to repentance. It presents a jurisprudential ruling attributed to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام within the chapter on the hadd of the apostate and female apostate.
